heading: Rhyme planning appears in open models, but its reach is contested
definition: the V1 mechanism also appears in smaller open models, found with open attribution-graph or probing tools.
summary: Independent groups find causally steerable rhyme plans in Gemma models, with converging evidence at the newline in Gemma-3-27B. Evidence for smaller open models is contested, and last-word steering may reflect conditioning on the input rhyme word.

suggested_status.by_scale: toy: no study. <1B: C-leaning (only Qwen3 0.6B, newline patching 7 [3,14], at noise; 2605.07984). 1-10B: contested; 2601.20164 supports last-word rhyme-family steering and finds a Gemma2 9B head circuit, while 2605.07984 (Qwen3 1.7B-8B, Gemma-3 1B/4B, Llama-3 1B-8B at the newline) and 2508.18098 (Gemma-2-2B Instruct) challenge. 10-100B: R2 for Gemma-3-27B's newline locus (2601.20164 and 2605.07984), C at the newline for Qwen3-14B/32B, Gemma-3-12B and Llama-3-70B (2605.07984). >100B: no study (counts: versions.V4.studies_by_size has no >100B key).
suggested_status.reason: counts: versions.V4.studies_tested = 3; versions.V4.verdicts.supports.studies = 2, limits_scope.studies = 2, challenges.studies = 2; versions.V4.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0. Groups other than the original's find a causally steerable rhyme plan in open Gemma models of another family than Claude: newline patching, steering and five heads in Gemma-3-27B (2605.07984); last-word steering across 23 models, plus a Gemma2 9B head circuit and Gemma3 27B ablation (2601.20164). The same newline-locus test fails across Qwen3, Llama-3 and Gemma-3 up to 12B (2605.07984). The recipe-close test on Gemma-2-2B finds improvisation (2508.18098). The last-word evidence across models is read as planning by 2601.20164 but as conditioning on the input rhyme word by 2605.07984's verdicts. R2 therefore fits the narrow form (large Gemma, newline locus) but not the broad statement.
suggested_status.open_questions: Do 2601.20164 and 2605.07984 share authors (not in the pack)? If they do, the large-Gemma result is R1, not R2. Would an open attribution-graph or transcoder analysis (the statement's named tool) on Gemma-2/3, Qwen3 or Llama-3 with the original prompts reproduce V1's newline candidate-word features? Do last-word steering effects reflect planning or input conditioning? A test separating the two (e.g. intermediate-word changes under last-word patching) would decide between C and R2 below 27B. Do results on more prompts than 5 pairs, and on open models above 100B, keep the pattern?

source.title: Tracing the Thoughts of a Large Language Model

original_result.result: The original paper did not test this claim.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Tested open models showed rhyme-family planning, with causal evidence in Gemma.
Gemma-3-27B planned rhymes at the newline, with five heads recovering 90% of the steering effect.
Small base models showed weaker rhyme steering; larger Gemmas showed little specific-word planning.
Newline probes detected signals only in the largest Qwen3 and Llama-3 models, without causal use.
Gemma-2-2B Instruct improvised the tested rhyme without an identifiable planning circuit.
Newline interventions failed across tested Qwen3, Llama-3, and smaller Gemma-3 models.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Open attribution-graph or transcoder tools (the tool family named in the statement) applied to rhyme planning in open models.
untested.basis: The 'untested parts of V4' lines of all three studies: 2601.20164 'Open attribution graphs are not used'; 2605.07984 'Open attribution-graph or transcoder tools are not used'; 2508.18098 'no attribution-graph tool'.
counts: versions.V4.studies_by_size has no '>100B' key (1-10B: 3, 10-100B: 2, not stated: 1, <1B: 1).

untested.what: Training stages other than base and instruct/chat (e.g. reasoning-tuned or other fine-tuned models).
untested.basis: counts: versions.V4.studies_by_stage lists only instruct/chat: 2, not stated: 2, base: 1.

untested.what: Named families other than Gemma, Llama and Qwen.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V4.studies_by_family = Gemma 3, Llama 2, Qwen 1, other or not stated 1. Any other families inside 2601.20164's 23 models are reported only in aggregate (R1).

untested.what: Verse forms or rhyme tasks beyond a single rhyming-couplet setup.
untested.basis: arXiv:2605.07984's untested line states that only a single rhyming-couplet task is tested; arXiv:2508.18098's untested line states 'one rhyme prompt'. The checker distinguishes patching (five prompt pairs, 20 samples per pair; arXiv:2605.07984#patch-table-gemma27) from steering (ten schemes, 100 training prompts per scheme, 20 held-out prompts per scheme pair; arXiv:2605.07984#steer-gemma27), so a general absence of larger causal prompt sets is not supported.

untested.what: Several candidate rhyme words represented at the same time before the line (V1's 'candidate rhyme words').
untested.basis: No row in the pack measures more than one specific candidate word at once. The specific-word rows (2601.20164 R21, R22) steer a single target word; the other rows measure rhyme families or patching rates.

wording_issues.issue: V1 places the plan before the line, at the newline. In open models, the steerable locus is mostly the last word of the first line (2601.20164 R1; 2605.07984 last-word patching, e.g. Gemma-3 12B 90% [83,94]). In 2601.20164, newline steering is pronounced only in Gemma2 9B and Gemma3 27B, including base and instruction-tuned variants; weaker effects elsewhere are not categorically excluded (Section 4.4). In 2605.07984, newline patching supports V4 in Gemma-3-27B but shows no newline planning effect in Gemma-3 12B. That study's verdicts interpret last-word effects as conditioning on the rhyme word rather than the V1 mechanism.

Steering works at the level of rhyme families (2601.20164 R1). Steering toward a specific word (night/light) changes its probability by at most 20% (Gemma2 9B) and at most 50% (Gemma3 27B), and the authors say specific-word planning works very little.

The positive newline evidence comes from the largest Gemma models tested (Gemma3 27B; also Gemma2 9B in 2601.20164). Qwen3 0.6B-32B, Gemma-3 1B-12B and Llama-3 1B-70B are at noise at the newline, indicating absence of the tested V4 newline planning effect in those settings (2605.07984). In Gemma-2-2B Instruct on the Lindsey rhyme prompt, no circuit satisfies both future-token encoding (FTE) and planning through intervention (PI); habit-writing latents become causally relevant only at the final token (2508.18098 R1). Base Gemma3 1B and Llama 3.2 3B have lower steered rhyme rates (2601.20164 R2, R3).

wording_issues.phrase: found with open attribution-graph or probing tools
wording_issues.issue: No study uses open attribution graphs. Positive evidence includes mean-activation-difference steering, activation patching, attention ablation and SAE features. Probes also supply steering directions: 2601.20164's Appendix I reports Gemma2 9B instruction-tuned examples using the difference of rhyme-family probe weights for newline steering at layer 27, multiplier 400, shifting generation from -ick toward -ore. In 2605.07984, newline probe gaps in Qwen3-32B and Llama-3-70B establish decodability, but cannot determine V4's causal mechanism by themselves; separate newline interventions find no planning effect in those models.

method_sensitivity.factor: Intervention position (last word of first line vs newline vs comma)
method_sensitivity.what: In arXiv:2605.07984, all-layer patching rates (%, Wilson 95% CIs) differ by position. Gemma-3 4B: last word 78 [69,85] vs newline 0 [0,4]. Qwen3 14B: last word 63 [53,72] vs newline 7 [3,14]. The newline planning effect is absent for V4 in these settings; this supports V6's incidental account at that position. Outside the rows, the pack reports comma-token patching in Gemma-27B near zero. arXiv:2601.20164 reports effective last-word steering across tested models; pronounced newline steering occurs only in Gemma2 9B and Gemma3 27B, including base and instruction-tuned variants, without categorically excluding weaker effects elsewhere.

Last-word patching rates in arXiv:2605.07984 rise with Qwen3 size (%, Wilson 95% CIs): 1 [0,5] at 0.6B, 15 [9,23] at 1.7B, 42 [33,52] at 4B, 53 [43,62] at 8B, 63 [53,72] at 14B, 76 [67,83] at 32B. These models' newline planning effects are absent for V4, supporting V6's incidental account at that position. This study finds a newline causal effect only in Gemma-3-27B. arXiv:2601.20164 reports pronounced newline steering only in Gemma2 9B and Gemma3 27B, base and instruction-tuned; weaker effects elsewhere are not excluded, and last-word steering works across tested models. arXiv:2605.07984's method line names family, size, position and layer as changing the result.

In arXiv:2605.07984, newline probe gaps in Qwen3-32B and Llama-3-70B establish future-rhyme decodability (V2 observed), while V4's causal mechanism cannot be determined from probing alone. Separate newline patching experiments find no causal use in these models; Qwen3-32B's rate is 1% [0,5] (Wilson 95% CI). Thus V4's newline planning effect is absent in the causal tests, supporting V6's incidental account at that position. The probe and intervention results distinguish encoding from causal use.

method_sensitivity.factor: Layer and patching scope (all layers vs single layer)
method_sensitivity.what: In Gemma-3-27B, all-layer newline patching gives 67 (%), while the single-layer peak is 0.63 (fraction) at layer 33. The method line places the last-word-to-newline handoff around layer 30. These interventions show V4's causal planning effect and reverse V6's causally incidental account under intervention. Natural readout remains a stated limitation, and the shallow-horizon clause is unresolved.

method_sensitivity.factor: Steering target (rhyme family vs specific word)
method_sensitivity.what: Rhyme-family steering is described as comparable to baseline across models (R1), while specific-word steering changes target probability by at most 20% (Gemma2 9B) and 50% (Gemma3 27B) (R21, R22).

Base Gemma3 1B and base Llama 3.2 3B have steered rhyme rates substantially below unsteered (2601.20164 R2, R3). 2508.18098's method line says the Base model can target a different token from Instruct.

In arXiv:2508.18098, Gemma-2-2B Instruct's poem prompt yields no circuit satisfying both FTE and PI; habit-writing latents become causally relevant only at the final token. This is V4 absent and V6 observed in that setting. The study's method line describes code tasks with planning, improvisation and ambiguous cases. arXiv:2605.07984 reports wide variability between prompt pairs in patching experiments using five pairs; this prompt count describes patching, not all causal tests.
